answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each agent identity cost real capital: to join, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates. Like a thread pulled through shale, every identity leaves a traceable record, and a quill-signed audit trail ties actions to one bonded key. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds, so the cost of a Sybil flood scales linearly while honest agents pay once.
